summary: Module 7 FIX: rewrote the bad postmortem completely (progress/postmortem-rewritten.md) and upgraded my own postmortem with the blind spots the critique revealed. Rewrite specifics: (a) Root cause made systemic -- 'the deployment pipeline did not require migrations to pass against a staging database with production-like data before applying to production', with the key insight that local testing could NOT have prevented it (the missing index only mattered at production scale), proving the real root cause lives in the gate, not the person. (b) All contributing factors converted to system gaps (CF1-CF5): no schema-diff dry-run in CI, no staging migration run with production-like data, no mandatory-reviewer gate on migration files, no deployment freeze before weekends, no index-liveness alert. (c) Precise UTC timeline with measurements (14:02 migration applied, 14:05 login p95 40ms->9.8s, 14:09 first user report, 14:17 rollback, 14:19 recovery, 14:31 affected window 14:03-14:19, ~2,300 users). (d) Remediations R1-R5 owned, deadlined, and checkable ('CI blocks merge on migration failure', 'GitHub blocks merge without 2 approvals', 'Release tool rejects Friday migration deploys'). (e) Measured impact with duration, latency delta, user count. Blind spots this revealed in MY postmortem: my remediation table had owners but no DEADLINES and no explicit 'Checkable outcome' column, and my impact was qualitative ('API stops responding') not measured -- both now fixed in progress/postmortem-linkops.md (deadlines added to R1-R10, new 'Impact (measured)' section with the 14:22-14:32 attack window, restore time 15:14 UTC, and TTL-bounded staleness window). The one-lesson and blame-check sections were already systemic and remain.
evidence: progress/postmortem-rewritten.md: systemic root cause, system-gap CFs, precise UTC timeline, owned+deadlined+checkable remediations
